answer.rationale: Onset lines up with the release (shipped ~30 minutes before latency started climbing). memory_b1 is the closest prior control: rollback cleared a checkout incident on a known-stable build without customer impact, which matches the objective of keeping customer writes. Failover (memory_b2) remains plausible because the symptom is regional write latency, but shifting the write path during peak settlement risks in-flight or split-brain write loss, so it is not the first move. Circuit breaking (memory_b4) would fail writes and is incompatible with the objective. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) treated reporting load, not the write path. Daily settlement peak is expected load; memory_b3 was pre-peak headroom, not a mid-incident write-path fix. Causal uncertainty remains (release vs primary-region saturation), so rollback is scoped as a standard guarded revert rather than a broader cutover. Settlement-peak write mutation is flagged as downstream value risk.
